mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 YoY < -2% and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between INDPRO 3-month decline >1% and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample data.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall >3% MoM
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between joint GDPC1/HOUST >3% MoM declines and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when PAYEMS > 12-mo avg and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average, while consumption (GDPC1) remains flat, indicates households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which reduces near-term demand and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo avg AND GDPC1 flat (change < 0.5% QoQ)
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between RSAFS > 12-mo avg with flat GDPC1 and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample.
